text: Two case studies are built. Now the question that matters six months from now: how does the next person understand what you built, without you standing next to them?

The builder always leaves, eventually -- a new role, a different team, or just a faded memory. What's left behind is either a document that answers the obvious questions, or an automation the next admin has to carefully reverse-engineer by clicking through Setup.
Five things, every time: the purpose in one sentence, the exact trigger or entry criteria, who it affects, what it depends on, and who owns it with a last-reviewed date.

Applied to Lesson 11's quote approval, that's under ten lines -- purpose, trigger, who's affected, dependencies, and an owner. Anyone inheriting it can answer 'what would break if I changed this' without opening Setup first.
A document nobody knows to look for isn't really a handoff -- it's just a file. Real handoff means a predictable location, plus an actual walkthrough with whoever takes over.
Next lesson moves from reading designs to building one yourself, start to finish, in a hands-on practice lab.
